newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom says falling ringgit affecting profits.
newsitem.headline: Telekom says falling ringgit affecting profits.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd said the continued depreciation of the ringgit against the U.S. dollar is affecting its bottomline as the company is exposed to foreign loans.
At the dollar/ringgit level of 2.80, the company was incurring a foreign exchange loss of 60 million ringgit, said Telekom's corporate treasurer Ghazali Harun at the weekend.
But as long as there were no payments to be made on the company's offshore loans, the losses would not be realised, he told reporters after an analysts' briefing.
On Friday, the ringgit fell to 2.8250 to the dollar, its weakest level since it was officially floated in 1973. But it staged a sharp recovery to 2.7780 before the end of the day.
The ringgit had lost 13 percent of its value against the dollar over the past month following speculative attacks on regional currencies.
The next payment Telekom is due to make is on its offshore bonds issue at the end of September.
Telekom has issued a $360 million Euro bond and a $500 million Yankee bond.
Ghazali said Telekom was closely monitoring the ringgit's movement against the dollar and would make the necessary hedging at the right time.
On plans to raise $350 million in offshore bonds to part finance Telekom's investment in South Africa's Telkom, Ghazali said the company was still arranging for a long term financing package.
The company recently bought a 12 percent stake in Telkom for $504 million.
